assessment.rationale: Held: the Main KPI of 3,000 cell types catalogued is already met by an open resource. Siletti et al. (Science 2023) profiled more than three million nuclei from about 100 dissections of the adult human brain and identified 31 superclusters, 461 clusters and 3,313 subclusters (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=TITLE%3A%22Transcriptomic%20diversity%20of%20cell%20types%20across%20the%20adult%20human%20brain%22&format=json&pageSize=3&resultType=core). That census and its mouse counterpart are distributed as an open science resource: the Allen Brain Cell Atlas carries the human taxonomy (3,313 subclusters), the whole mouse brain atlas (about 4 million cells, 5,322 clusters), MERFISH whole mouse brain (about 9 million cells, over 5,000 clusters) and SEA-AD, explorable in the browser and downloadable from GitHub with programmatic access (https://brain-map.org/atlases-and-data/bkp/abc-atlas). The count the project asks for therefore exists today, free, from a discoverable source. Honest limits, stated plainly: these are transcriptomic taxonomies, so the second half of the project title, cell functions, is not delivered by them; Siletti's census rests on three postmortem donors; cluster counts are taxonomy-dependent rather than a settled number of types; and the atlas effort continues into new modalities, for example an MRI-guided whole mouse brain cell-type atlas at 10 micrometre resolution (Commun Biol 2026) (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=TITLE%3A%22whole%20mouse%20brain%22%20AND%20TITLE%3A%22cell%20type%22%20AND%20atlas&format=json&pageSize=3&resultType=core). A reframed project on functional annotation of named human cell types, with a falsifiable endpoint, would be open work and would need its own prior-art basis. As written this is not opened as new work.

additionalSearches.query: adult human brain cell type census
additionalSearches.finding: Siletti et al., Science 2023 (eadd7046): single-nucleus RNA sequencing of more than three million nuclei from about 100 dissections in three postmortem donors, yielding 461 clusters and 3,313 subclusters. The KPI figure of 3,000 catalogued cell types is already exceeded in the published record.

additionalSearches.query: Allen Brain Cell Atlas contents and access
additionalSearches.finding: The ABC Atlas is described as an open science resource holding the Yao 2023 whole mouse brain atlas (about 4 million cells; 34 classes, 338 subclasses, 1,201 supertypes, 5,322 clusters), Zhuang MERFISH whole mouse brain (about 9 million cells, over 5,000 clusters), the Siletti human atlas (3,313 subclusters) and SEA-AD, with browser exploration, GitHub download and programmatic access.

additionalSearches.query: whole mouse brain cell type atlas publications
additionalSearches.finding: An MRI-guided whole mouse brain neuronal cell-type atlas at 10 micrometre isotropic resolution (Communications Biology 2026, open access, with a 2025 bioRxiv preprint) shows the field has moved on to spatial and anatomical registration of the existing taxonomies rather than to counting more types.

additionalSearches.query: open-source brain cell atlas analysis repositories
additionalSearches.finding: Five small repositories (cross-species substance-use atlas, pig brain atlas code, mosquito brain atlas code, a SEA-AD graph neural network, a Human Protein Atlas gene-set explorer). The open answer here is the atlas data and portal rather than community code.
